results.title: US: Protesters demand human control over AI after Anthropic's IPO
results.content: Protesters gathered outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters on 19 November 2026 to demand tighter regulation and greater human control over artificial intelligence, following the company’s $2 trillion stock market debut.

results.title: Japan: The dark secret behind an island paradise full of rabbits
results.content: Hundreds of rabbits roam freely on Japan's Okunoshima Island, delighting visitors from around the world. But behind its idyllic scenery lies a troubling history of secret chemical weapons production.

results.title: Ukraine: Kyiv metro stations become overnight shelters amid air raids
results.content: Residents of Kyiv, Ukraine, sought refuge in underground metro stations overnight on Thursday 19 November 2026, as repeated air raid alerts warned of further Russian attacks on the capital. Strikes on the Ukrainian capital killed at least one person, injured five and damaged two embassies.

results.content: Russian strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv on Thursday. Windows were shattered and vehicles damaged, but diplomatic staff escaped unharmed.

results.title: Greenpeace protests at COP31, demands climate finance as island nations face growing threats
results.content: Greenpeace activists are staging a protest at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, demanding urgent action. Small island nations are also raising their voices, warning that the climate crisis threatens their very survival. But Greenpeace says progress at the negotiations remains far too slow.

results.title: 48 teams, 104 matches: FIFA U-17 World Cup kicks off in Qatar
results.content: Qatar is hosting the FIFA U-17 Men’s World Cup, which kicked off on 19 November 2026. It is the second time the country has staged the tournament, following its first hosting in 2025.

results.title: Uganda start U17 World Cup campaign with 3-0 defeat to South Korea
results.content: Uganda’s Under-17 side, the Uganda Cranes, opened their Group B campaign with a 3-0 defeat to South Korea on Thursday.

results.title: Zimbabwe destroys 250,000 landmines, but funding threatens 2030 clearance goal
results.content: A major milestone in Zimbabwe's efforts to clear deadly remnants of war. The HALO Trust, the world's largest landmine clearance charity, says it has destroyed 250,000 landmines across the country since 2013.

results.title: Canary island erects field hospital amid migrant influx
results.content: A sharp rise in migrant arrivals is putting pressure on health services on Spain's Canary Island of El Hierro. Authorities have set up a field hospital at a temporary reception centre to cope with demand. Around 11,000 migrants have arrived since the start of November.

results.title: US: Protesters warn of AI bubble as Anthropic makes stock market history
results.content: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut with a record-breaking IPO valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. Outside the exchange in New York, police detained three protesters warning of financial risks.

results.title: Gambia pays tribute to Rohingya after ICJ genocide ruling against Myanmar
results.content: Gambia on Thursday welcomed the landmark judgement of the International Court of Justice that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority. Gambia brought the case to the UN’s top court in 2019, two years after Myanmar’s military crackdown against the predominantly Muslim Rohingya.

results.title: 'Our culture and identity': Deaf Nigerians fight to preserve indigenous sign languages
results.content: While some are spoken by small communities, Hausa has emerged as a lingua franca among deaf people in northern Nigeria. "It is our culture and identity," says Umaru Zayyanu, Deaf sign language interpreter.

results.title: Somalia expels UAE Ambassador as diplomatic tensions escalate
results.content: Somalia has expelled the United Arab Emirates ambassador, escalating diplomatic tensions between the two countries. The Somali government accuses Abu Dhabi of interfering in its internal affairs.
